page: Microsoft Azure D64als_v6 is an x86_64 server instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at up to 3.7 GHz, the instance supplies 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory subsystem provides 128 GB of RAM, resulting in a 2 GB per core allocation. The AMD microarchitecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction set support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, alongside AES, VAES, and SHA cryptographic accelerators.

The hardware configuration features no bundled local storage and requires external Azure Premium Storage for persistent file systems and operating system disks. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPUs is not available, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided. The 1:2 core-to-memory ratio designates the D64als_v6 as a compute-dense variant within Azure's general-purpose lineup, trading per-core RAM capacity for higher thread density per memory allocation.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational capabilities, led by a top-tier multi-core Geekbench score of 21,957 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 98,446.73. The instance achieved 75,747.71 points in PassMark CPU testing and delivered high parallel compilation throughput with a Clang score of 53,868. Memory bandwidth measures 4,863.42 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 108.42 GB/sec for large block writes, though uncached large-block read bandwidth settles in the middle tier at 151.3 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the low-memory configuration optimizes resource utilization for processing tasks that do not require standard 4 GB per vCPU allocations. The server fits high-throughput compute jobs, software build pipelines, static web serving clusters, and batch data processing workloads where parallel integer and floating-point throughput takes priority over expansive memory footprints.
description: Microsoft Azure D64als_v6 is a compute-focused instance within the Dalv6 series, featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running up to 3.7 GHz. The system provides 128 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 2 GB per vCPU ratio, with AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions. It contains no bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying on remote persistent storage solutions. Multi-threaded benchmark testing places the instance in the upper tiers of general compute performance, showing strong metrics in Geekbench, stress-ng, and Clang compilation tasks. Memory bandwidth is solid for write operations, though uncached read bandwidth remains average. By limiting memory capacity relative to thread count, the D64als_v6 delivers cost-effective parallel processing power suited for continuous integration build farms, batch computing, static web traffic, and microservice hosts.
